related_questions.question: What are the current recommendations for treating COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: Current COVID-19 treatment protocols include antiviral medications and supportive care. Oral antiviral pills like Nirmatrelvir with Ritonavir (Paxlovid) and Molnupiravir (Lagevrio) are used for those at high risk, while intravenous Remdesivir (Veklury) is administered in healthcare facilities. Supportive care focuses on managing symptoms and preventing complications.

list.snippet: Nirmatrelvir with Ritonavir (Paxlovid): A combination pill for adults and children 12 years and older who are at high risk of severe illness, taken orally at home.
Molnupiravir (Lagevrio): Another oral antiviral option for adults at high risk, also taken at home.
Remdesivir (Veklury): Administered intravenously in a healthcare facility for three consecutive days, for adults and children at high risk.
This includes measures to manage symptoms like fever, cough, and fatigue, and may involve oxygen therapy or other interventions to prevent complications.
For those with severe illness, hospitalization and advanced respiratory support might be necessary.

list.title: Who is eligible for treatment:
list.snippet: Treatment is typically recommended for individuals at high risk of developing severe COVID-19, such as those with underlying medical conditions, older adults, and those who are immunocompromised.

list.title: When to seek treatment:
list.snippet: It's crucial to seek medical advice and treatment as soon as possible after testing positive for COVID-19, especially if you are at high risk.

list.title: Consult with a healthcare professional:
list.snippet: The specific treatment plan will be determined by a healthcare professional based on individual factors and the severity of the illness, according to the CDC.
